open_points.subject: reopened State 0 acceptance
open_points.text: “State 0 closes again when its question rounds are clear; the owner then accepts it as a whole” conflicts with “None open” and contains no later statement that the reopened whole was accepted.
open_points.question: Is the R0-24–R0-60 revision closed and accepted as the authoritative State 0, or is owner acceptance still pending?
options: Declare the revised State 0 accepted as a whole
Keep State 0 reopened and identify what remains before acceptance
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as still reopened and not yet accepted.

open_points.subject: service writes to Registry-owned identity
open_points.text: “Every other service names a project by the Registry's identity and reads that identity as a snapshot; none of them writes it back” conflicts with Cabinet Kernel being allowed to “add a room”, while rooms are part of Registry-owned project identity.
open_points.question: Is Kernel's agent-authority addition of rooms an intentional exception to the rule that other services never write Registry identity?
options: State the room-write exception explicitly
Restrict room creation to the owner
Define rooms as outside the identity that services may not write
open_points.default_guess: State Cabinet Kernel's granted-session room addition as an explicit exception.

open_points.subject: per-source migration closure
open_points.text: “Registry stores only identity … project access … pending request, artifact pointers, and its own audit log” omits the fact required by “Each source's first successful import into production closes the operation for that source”.
open_points.question: What authoritative fact tells Registry that the VPS or test-rig import has already succeeded and must now be refused?
options: Store explicit per-source migration-completion state
Derive completion from immutable audit entries
Close each source through deployment configuration outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Store an explicit completion flag for each declared source.

open_points.subject: owner sign-in
open_points.text: “Every request on either is authenticated; anything not authenticated is refused” conflicts with “The owner signs in to the owner interface with the owner credential”, because the initial sign-in request cannot already have an authenticated owner session.
open_points.question: Which owner-interface requests may be answered before authentication, and what may they return?
options: Allow only the sign-in form and sign-in submission before authentication
Use an external authentication layer so every Registry request is already authenticated
Treat unauthenticated requests as redirects without returning Registry data
open_points.default_guess: Allow only the sign-in flow and non-sensitive supporting responses before authentication.

open_points.subject: Cabinet Web mirror network path
open_points.text: “The Cabinet Web mirror … keeps its read only if it receives a token of its own” is not reconciled with the service API being reachable only inside VM Platform and over the VPS WireGuard channel used by Client Portal.
open_points.question: Where does the Cabinet Web mirror run, and through which permitted network boundary can it reach Registry?
options: Run it inside VM Platform
Run it on the VPS over the existing WireGuard channel
Retire its Registry access
open_points.default_guess: Retire its Registry access unless it is placed inside VM Platform.

open_points.subject: reads after project anonymisation
open_points.text: “read a project” returns any-status project “with its object”, and R0-45 says “context therefore always has an address”, but anonymisation makes “its name, object and customer link go” while `validate` still answers `archived`.
open_points.question: What do project-card and `context` reads return for an anonymised archived project whose required object and address no longer exist?
options: Refuse project-card and context reads while leaving validate and artifact reads available
Return a declared tombstone shape without object or address
Change anonymisation so a non-identifying object/context value survives
open_points.default_guess: Return a distinct archived-anonymised tombstone and refuse the full context contract.

open_points.subject: migration completion scope
open_points.text: The import action says “after the first successful production import the operation is closed and refused”, while R0-54 and R0-59 say the migration closes separately for the VPS and the test rig.
open_points.question: Does one successful import close all migration, or may the VPS and test rig each be imported successfully once?
options: Close separately per source
Close all imports after the first success
open_points.default_guess: Close separately per source, as R0-54 and R0-59 state.

open_points.subject: declined access request outcome
open_points.text: “declining changes nothing; the session reads the outcome in its access” does not say how a decline is observable, because the access output contains only granted project ids, the active project and the access version.
open_points.question: How does the session distinguish a declined request from a still-pending request or an unchanged access set?
options: Include pending/request outcome in the access read
Expose a separate request-status read
Treat disappearance of the pending request plus an access-version change as the outcome
open_points.default_guess: Include the pending request's status in the session-access response.

open_points.subject: answering an access request
open_points.text: “declining changes nothing” conflicts with “a request no longer pending refused”; answering must at least clear or resolve the pending request.
open_points.question: What state transition occurs when the owner declines a pending request?
options: Mark the request declined and retain its outcome
Remove the pending request without retaining an outcome
Leave it pending, making repeated answers possible
open_points.default_guess: Mark it declined, clear it as pending and retain the outcome for the session to read.

open_points.subject: unknown agent session
open_points.text: “an unknown session answers that it has no access” and the access-request failure “—” conflict with R0-53: “A call naming a session that is not registered is refused … an access request included”.
open_points.question: How must `read the session's access` and `request access` behave when Kernel names an unregistered session?
options: Refuse both exactly like other unregistered-session calls
Return empty access for reads but refuse requests
Return empty access and accept a request that implicitly registers the session

open_points.subject: agent operation without project id or active project
open_points.text: The active project is “the default when the agent names none”, but it may be absent or cleared and no failure is given for an agent-authority operation that supplies no `project_id` in that state.
open_points.question: What happens when an agent operation omits `project_id` and the session has no active project?
options: Refuse with the same non-disclosing failure used for unavailable projects
Require `project_id` whenever no active project exists
Choose from the granted set automatically
open_points.default_guess: Refuse without selecting a project automatically.

open_points.subject: session access version
open_points.text: “read the session's access” returns “the access version”, but no text says which actions advance it or whether owner changes must state the version they were made against.
open_points.question: What is the access version for, which grant, revoke, active-project, request or session-lifecycle changes advance it, and are stale access changes refused?
options: Use it as an optimistic-concurrency revision for all session-access changes
Use it only as a monotonically changing observation token
Remove it from the State 0 output promise
open_points.default_guess: Use it as a revision advanced by every accepted change to grants or the active project, with stale owner changes refused.

open_points.subject: discovering sessions and pending access requests
open_points.text: “the owner sees [a registered session] in the owner interface” and sees a session's pending request, but the action list has only a read for one already-known session and no action to list registered sessions or pending requests.
open_points.question: Through which Registry action does the owner discover registered sessions and their pending requests so they can grant access or answer a request?
options: Add an owner action listing sessions with pending-request state
Add separate session-list and pending-request-list actions
Require Kernel or another external component to supply the session identifiers
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner-only session list that includes each session's pending-request status.

open_points.subject: deleting a project that remains in session access
open_points.text: “erase an archived project” may delete it whole, while archiving “keeps it in a [session] set”; no text says whether whole deletion removes that id from granted sets or clears it as an active project.
open_points.question: What happens to every agent session grant and active-project reference when an archived project is deleted whole?
options: Atomically remove the project from every granted set and clear affected active projects
Keep dangling grants that behave exactly like nonexistent projects
Refuse deletion until all session grants are revoked
open_points.default_guess: Atomically remove the deleted project from all session access and clear it wherever active.

open_points.subject: restriction exceptions
open_points.text: “any operation using its restricted personal data is refused unless the law provides an exception” does not name who decides that an exception applies, what input conveys it, or which operation records or checks it; R0-60 also says Registry keeps no holdbacks.
open_points.question: How can Registry determine that an operation on restricted contact data is legally excepted?
options: Define a fixed set of owner operations allowed during restriction
Require an explicit owner assertion or confirmation for each exceptional operation
Keep all such processing outside Registry and permit no operational exception
open_points.default_guess: Define a fixed, narrow set of owner-only operations allowed while restricted and refuse all others.

open_points.subject: customer record deletion
open_points.text: R0-57 says “Until its record is deleted the owner may resume the relationship”, but the only customer erasure action keeps the Customer identity and erased fact, and no action deletes a Customer record.
open_points.question: Can a Customer record ever be deleted whole; if so, by what action and with what effects on projects that name it?
options: Add whole-customer deletion with defined referential effects
Declare Customer tombstones permanent and remove the reference to record deletion
Delete the record as part of contact-data erasure once no project links remain
open_points.default_guess: Keep permanent erased tombstones and remove the unsupported record-deletion possibility.

open_points.subject: personal data in the agent projection
open_points.text: The agent projection includes “display name, … rooms and artifact pointers — no address, customer or other personal value”, but those caller-supplied names, room names, `uri` and `payload_ref` values are not constrained from containing personal data.
open_points.question: What enforces the promise that the projection never exposes personal data embedded in project names, room names or artifact references?
options: Forbid and validate personal data in every projected field
Redact or replace unsafe values before returning the projection
Classify these fields as potentially personal and remove them from agent output
open_points.default_guess: Constrain projected fields to non-personal values and reject violating writes where enforceable.

open_points.subject: audit event coverage
open_points.text: “only significant changes of state” is followed by a partial category list, leaving room additions, artifact publication and withdrawal, session registration, active-project changes, access requests and rejected changes unresolved; the audit schema also includes “the outcome” although failed operations make no state change.
open_points.question: Exactly which accepted and refused primary actions create audit entries?
options: Audit every state-changing primary action and its refusal
Audit only the explicitly enumerated project, customer, grant, revoke, restriction and erasure events
Declare an explicit per-action audit matrix
open_points.default_guess: Declare a per-action matrix and audit every accepted durable state change plus security-relevant refused changes.

open_points.subject: onboard_object authentication and lifecycle
open_points.text: The exclusion calls `onboard_object` “a client of the API like any consumer” while saying its staff credential ends and its role is taken by the owner interface and Kernel flows; owner credentials are held by no tool and project creation is owner-only.
open_points.question: Is `onboard_object` retired, or does it retain any authenticated Registry operation under a newly named authority?
options: Retire it and state that it no longer calls vNext Registry
Give it a dedicated service identity and enumerate its allowed operations
Make it an owner-interface wrapper that never holds credentials itself
